    • SMC_KEYS_CPU_TEMP_AGGREGATE_AS

      public static final List<String> SMC_KEYS_CPU_TEMP_AGGREGATE_AS
      Apple Silicon CPU-die aggregate temperature keys, tried in order until one returns a plausible value. These are computed by the SMC firmware and are chip-independent, unlike the per-core SMC_KEYS_CPU_TEMP_AS keys which vary between chips (and are entirely absent on some, e.g. the M3 Pro). TCMb is the CPU-die average and TCMz is the CPU-die maximum; the average is preferred because it stays close to the single-sensor value OSHI historically reported.

    • SMC_KEYS_CPU_TEMP_AS

    • SMC_KEYS_GPU_TEMP_AS

      public static final List<String> SMC_KEYS_GPU_TEMP_AS
      Fallback Apple Silicon GPU temperature keys, used only when runtime discovery cannot complete. The hottest plausible reading among them is reported.

      GPU sensor keys are chip-specific, so no fixed list is complete: on an M2 Max only Tg0f and Tg0j of the four originally shipped exist, and six of that machine's sensors appear in no published key table at all. getGpuTemperatureKeys() therefore discovers them from the SMC instead; this list is breadth-first insurance for the case where that fails. It leads with the four keys OSHI read before discovery existed, so the fallback can never report less than the previous implementation, followed by the keys most commonly present across published M1 through M5 and A18 sensor dumps.

    • MIN_PLAUSIBLE_TEMPERATURE

      public static final double MIN_PLAUSIBLE_TEMPERATURE
      The lowest reading accepted as a genuine temperature, in degrees Celsius.

      Apple Silicon power-gates a CPU core cluster when it is idle, and the SMC then reports a fixed sentinel for each die sensor in that cluster instead of a reading. Observed sentinels are 6.7 and 4.633 on an M2 Max (Tp01/Tp09 and Tp05/Tp0D), up to 8.425 across all of that machine's sensors, and -4.0 through 5.2 in the iSMC sample reports, which independently describe them as "firmware sentinels from inactive sensor slots". They are below room ambient and so cannot be real die temperatures, but most are positive, so a simple > 0 test accepts them.

      Across those reports, covering M1 through M5, A18 and Intel T2 machines, no genuine sensor read between 8.425 and 21, so this floor sits in an empty band with margin on both sides. It is a plausibility guard, not a hardware specification.

      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • smcGetMaxTemperature

      public static double smcGetMaxTemperature(IOKit.IOConnect conn, List<String> keys)
      Get the highest plausible temperature among a list of SMC keys.

      Plausibility is applied per read rather than when the keys were discovered, because whether a key exists is a property of the hardware while whether it currently reports a usable value is not.

      Clusters expose their sensors in pairs at different locations on the die, offset by a few degrees and tracking each other as load changes; verified on an M2 Max where a pair moved 44.8/51.4 to 56.1/62.6 under load and fell together afterwards. They are not an instantaneous/peak-hold pair, so taking the maximum consistently reports the hotter location rather than a latched peak.

      Parameters:
      conn - The connection
      keys - The keys to read
      Returns:
      The highest reading at or above MIN_PLAUSIBLE_TEMPERATURE, or 0 if none were plausible

    • getGpuTemperatureKeys

      public static List<String> getGpuTemperatureKeys()
      Get the Apple Silicon GPU temperature keys for this machine, discovering them from the SMC on first use and caching the result.

      Discovery binary searches the sorted key index for the Tg block and keeps the keys matching the GPU naming convention. It does not filter by plausibility: an idle sensor reports a sentinel below ambient, so filtering here would let one unlucky first call cache an empty set and disable GPU temperature permanently. Plausibility is applied per read by smcGetMaxTemperature(IOKit.IOConnect, List).

      Can be overridden with the GlobalConfig.OSHI_OS_MAC_SENSORS_GPUTEMPERATURE_KEYS configuration property, which bypasses discovery entirely. Falls back to SMC_KEYS_GPU_TEMP_AS if discovery cannot complete, without caching, so a later call retries.

      Returns:
      The keys to read for GPU temperature, never null

    • getFanSpeedKeys

      public static List<String> getFanSpeedKeys()
      Get the keys to read for fan speeds, discovering them from the SMC key index on first use and caching the result.

      The key index is authoritative about which keys exist, so it is preferred over the count FNum reports. A positive FNum still implies the conventionally named keys where discovery finds none, so this never reports fewer fans than reading FNum directly did. See SmcKeyIndex.reconcileFanKeys(java.util.List, long).

      Can be overridden with the GlobalConfig.OSHI_OS_MAC_SENSORS_FANSPEED_KEYS configuration property, which bypasses discovery entirely.

      Returns:
      The keys to read for fan speeds, never null

    • getCpuVoltageKeys

      public static List<String> getCpuVoltageKeys()
      Get the keys to read for CPU voltage, in the order they should be tried.

      Unlike the GPU temperature keys these are not discovered from the key index, because the V prefix is not specific to the CPU: an M3 Pro reports a 0.75 V core voltage from VP0C alongside a 20 V supply rail from VD0R, with no naming convention separating them. A prefix scan could therefore report a rail voltage as the CPU's, which is worse than reporting nothing. Use GlobalConfig.OSHI_OS_MAC_SENSORS_CPUVOLTAGE_KEYS to name the key on hardware where neither default works.

      Returns:
      The keys to read for CPU voltage, never null
